filename: A Self-Diagnosing Structural Error-Aware Parameter Estimation Method for Earth System Models.pdf
title: A Self-Diagnosing Structural Error-Aware Parameter Estimation Method for Earth System Models
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: The study generated a multi-iteration perturbed parameter ensemble (initial 100 members plus subsequent calibrated iterations) of CAM6 with an ML warm-rain scheme, perturbing 34 physical parameters, deposited on Zenodo with public code on GitHub. It directly suits benchmarking parameter estimation, structural error detection, and emulation algorithms.
pain_points: Structural error between observational targets (e.g. FLUT vs LWCF, PRECT vs radiative fluxes) where no parameter set matches both targets simultaneously
Sparsity in high-dimensional parameter space (100 ensemble members over 34 parameters)
Curse of dimensionality in GP emulation necessitating decomposition into 2D parameter subspaces
Risk of over-constraining and compensating for structural error if mismatch tolerances are inflated
Simulation failures during ensemble runs (e.g., 3 out of 90 runs failed in Iteration 1)
extraction_notes: The preprint date is marked as '14 Sep 2026' on arXiv (arXiv:2609.16210v1, submitted to JAMES). The host atmospheric model uses an online-coupled ML parameterization for warm rain microphysics based on a neural net trained from bin-resolved microphysics, inside CAM6. The calibration framework uses Gaussian Process emulators of 2-parameter projections and alpha shapes.
